note: Sources for the /last-mile page. 'limitations' states what each figure is not. Re-check before relying on any number.

sources.claim: U.S. online grocery sales rose 20.7% year over year in 3Q26. Delivery grew more than 30% and drove about three-quarters of the topline increase. Average order frequency among monthly active online grocery shoppers rose nearly 14% in the quarter.
sources.title: U.S. eGrocery Sales for 3Q26 Climb 21% Versus Last Year
sources.data_period: 3Q26 (monthly surveys in July, August and September 2026)
sources.measurement: Survey-based estimates from the Brick Meets Click Grocery Shopper Surveys: adults 18+ who take part in household grocery shopping, adjusted for internet usage, weighted by age and income to Census adult population figures. Delivery means orders from a first- or third-party provider; pickup; and ship-to-home via a common carrier.
sources.limitations: Survey-based grocery-sales estimates across fulfillment methods, not cold-chain logistics revenue, not a software market size, and not a count of refrigerated shipments. The page states no sample size or product-category coverage, and no total dollar amount for the quarter. 'Delivery' includes any grocery delivery, not only refrigerated or frozen items.

sources.claim: Monthly U.S. online grocery sales grew just over 16% year over year in September 2026. Average order frequency rose 9.0% year over year, and sub-same-day orders (within three hours of order placement) were about two-thirds of Delivery orders that month.
sources.title: Sept 2026: eGrocery sales up just over 16% year-over-year
sources.measurement: Brick Meets Click Grocery Shopping Survey. Order frequency is a year-over-year change in average orders per monthly active user. Average order value across delivery, pickup and ship-to-home was up 3.6% nominal; Delivery AOV fell 2.5%.
sources.limitations: A single month and a different period from the 3Q26 release, so its growth and order-frequency figures are not comparable to the quarterly ones. No dollar total, sample size or delivery/pickup order mix is given. Same grocery-wide scope as above, not refrigerated-only.

sources.claim: FDA, with USDA and CDC, highlighted best practices on food safety for third-party delivery services, covering mitigating measures for vulnerabilities including those that may arise in the 'last mile' of delivery, with topics including packaging, temperature control, contamination control and allergen control.
sources.title: FDA Highlights Best Practices on Food Safety for Online Delivery Services
sources.measurement: Guidance announcement (constituent update). It points to a Conference for Food Protection document; we have not read that document and have not verified its formal title.
sources.limitations: The page frames the content as recommendations and best practices, not a legal requirement, and does not list the individual recommendations or specific temperature or time limits. It addresses food, not pharmaceuticals. It is dated 2022; check for newer guidance.
